**BioNova Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**
Good morning, and welcome to the BioNova Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for Q&A instructions.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations:**
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BioNova Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. James Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Rachel Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Kevin Morales, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial; Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing; and Maria Lopez, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. James Harlan, CEO of BioNova Therapeutics.

**Dr. James Harlan, CEO:**
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. BioNova Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust volume growth in our oncology and rare disease franchises, alongside initial momentum from recent product launches. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, covering our overall performance highlights and key takeaways, clinical trial updates including phase progressions, data readouts, and regulatory milestones, new product launch updates and market share gains, strategic priorities and outlook, business development including licensing deals, acquisitions, and partnerships, the pricing and reimbursement landscape, patent cliff exposure and life cycle management strategies, and key assumptions and risk factors.

We are particularly excited about NovaTRK, our next-generation TRK inhibitor, and its potential to achieve peak U.S. sales of $2.2 billion annually by 2028, supported by expanded sales force efforts and favorable NCCN guidelines.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Thank you, Dr. Harlan. As Dr. Harlan mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $700 million, an increase of 20% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by the continued ramp-up of our flagship oncology asset NovaTRK, which we launched in the U.S. in Q1 following FDA accelerated approval based on Phase III CREST trial data showing a 68% objective response rate in ROS1-positive NSCLC patients, outperforming benchmarks from competitors like Roche's Rozlytrek, alongside strong contributions from our rare disease and gene therapy segments.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $120 million, or $0.85 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $180 million, or $1.28 per share.

Our operating expenses were $450 million, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D to support our pipeline while achieving SG&A efficiencies through AI-driven tools targeting a 15% reduction in promotional spend per script. We continue to invest heavily in R&D, with $850 million allocated this year, up 10% year-over-year, 60% to late-stage assets. Our cash position remains strong at $3.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to total revenue of $4.8 to $5.0 billion, representing 12-15% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, adjusted EPS of $5.50-5.80, reflecting oncology tailwinds, NeoVera ramp, and 2-3% forex headwind.

Thank you again, Dr. Harlan, and good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper into our outlook, let me walk you through our Q3 and full-year financial results to date, which underscore the resilience and momentum of BioNova Therapeutics as we navigate biosimilar erosion, U.S. pricing pressures from the Inflation Reduction Act, and softer emerging market demand due to currency volatility. Full-year revenue is tracking toward $2.48 billion, up 18% year-over-year on a reported basis and 20% at constant currency, well ahead of initial guidance. Q3 revenue hit $700 million, up 22% year-over-year, driven by volume in core oncology and rare diseases.

Breaking it down, our oncology portfolio, led by blockbuster PD-1 inhibitor ONCOvance, generated strong growth to around $1.35 billion year-to-date, up 25%, with U.S. net sales benefiting from expanded label in metastatic NSCLC from Phase III EXCEL-2 showing 28% PFS improvement. Ex-U.S., 15% growth despite some European biosimilar pressure. Rare disease and gene therapy surged 35% to $650 million year-to-date, fueled by U.S. launch of AAV-based GeneFix for SMA, with peak sales now at $1.2 billion, aligning with Novartis' Zolgensma trajectory, aided by North Carolina facility optimizations reducing COGS 12% quarter-over-quarter via single-use bioreactors. Legacy products and royalties flat at $480 million, offset by $75 million milestone from Bristol Myers Squibb on our JAK inhibitor.

Gross margin expanded to 82% year-to-date, up 300 basis points, due to high-margin biologics mix and supply chain efficiencies avoiding peer margin compression. Adjusted non-GAAP EPS at $4.85 year-to-date, up 28%, beating consensus by $0.15. GAAP EPS $3.42 after R&D impairments. Operating expenses up 12% to $1.6 billion, R&D at 28% of revenue funding 12 Phase III readouts and five NDAs in 2024, SG&A at 22% via AI patient adherence boosting ONCOvance persistency 15%. Free cash flow $850 million year-to-date, up 40%, enabling $400 million repurchases and $1 billion new authorization. Balance sheet fortress-like with net debt-to-EBITDA 1.2x.

Regionally, U.S. 65% of revenue at explosive 25% growth to $1.6 billion, ONCOvance at 32% 1L NSCLC share per IQVIA, GeneFix 45% vs. Spinraza. Europe 20% at 10% growth to $500 million, tempered by price concessions but AstraZeneca royalties at €300 million. Emerging markets 15% at 15% constant currency to $380 million, China via BeiGene JV, Brazil tenders.

Key trends: Capitalizing on GLP-1 boom with preclinical oral agonist to Phase II, mitigating $300 million patent cliffs via $2.5 billion M&A pipeline including $1.1 billion CAR-T tuck-in. AI/ML drug discovery screened 50,000 compounds yielding three INDs at 40% lower cost. Sustainability cut Scope 1 emissions 30%. Key takeaways: Innovation-first strategy with 20%+ CAGR, 45-asset pipeline 15 catalysts 2024, disciplined allocation with dividends up 10% to $0.80/share, resilient to macro with FY2024 guidance $2.9-3.1 billion revenue, 17-25% growth.

Turning to pricing and reimbursement, which drives our top-line in this dynamic environment. U.S. 68% of Q3 sales at $1.2 billion, gross-to-net 47% up from 44% YoY on higher PBM rebates, Express Scripts/CVS 55% lives. NovaCure WAC $185,000/year, Medicare ASP $162,000 down 4.2% on sequestration, biosimilars. Coverage 92% commercial, RWE shows 22% PFS edge vs. Keytruda. Medicare Advantage 28%, OBAs 15% lives tying rebates to PFS>65%, 8% leakage. 340B 18% volumes at 23-25% discount, copay caps via foundation preserved $120 million. Europe 22% €320 million, Germany PPMC 18% discount ASP €142,000 vs. France €110,000 22% clawback, JCA risks 5-7% ASP shave. Ex-China EM 7% $110 million, Brazil tenders 85% share 15% discount, China NRDL RMB 1.1 million 35% volume. Biosimilar readiness patent thickets to 2029, value-based UK NICE pilots, RWE $45 million. FY24 gross-to-net 45-48%, ASP flat U.S. down 2% Europe 4-5%, offset 12% volume.

On patent cliff exposure, top 10 products 78% $8.2 billion TTM revenue, three blockbusters LOE 2026-2030. Zylara GLP-1 $2.4 billion 35% U.S. T2D share, U.S. expiry 2028 EU 2030, 70-80% erosion $1.6-1.9 billion hit. OncoVirex PD-1 $1.8 billion 28% oncology, biosimilars 2027 60-75% loss. CardioShield PCSK9 $1.1 billion 2026 generics. U.S. 62% IRA tail, Europe faster uptake, EM 20-30% faster. LCM invested $450 million ROI 2.5x: label expansions Zylara obesity 15% $100B market +3 years exclusivity 12% Q3 uplift, OncoVirex three Ph3 combos to 2032. Formulations CardioShield monthly subQ to 2031 25% adherence 18% retention, Zylara oral Ph2 2029. Combos OncoVirex+CDK4/6 $800M peak. Pediatric/orphan/GSP extensions. M&A SynthoBio two Ph2 to 2035. Derisk $4.2B to $1.8B gap, payback 2029, R&D 22% gene editing/ADCs.

Business development cornerstone: Q3 three deals YTD upfronts $450M total $3.2B potential, 35% deal volume up. Licensing: in NVB-452 bispecific CD19/CD3 $150M upfront $850M milestones 18-24% royalties Ph2 78% ORR fills CAR-T gap BLA H2 2026 Eisai Japan. Out NVB-789 KRAS PROTAC $75M $600M royalties Sanofi Dupixent combos. Acquisitions $320M SynthoGenix AI antibodies ADCs SGX-114 IND Q4 60% efficiency Suzhou foothold. Tuck-ins <500M ROIC>25%. Partnerships CRISPR NVB-CRISPR-7 AATD 50/50 LNP Phase1 Q1 2025 $1.5B peak. Lonza $200M CTX capacity. AZ Ph2 bispecific combos $400M biobucks. Pillars pipeline 25% ADCs 15% gene editing, revenue 40% milestones 2025, 35% Asia hedge IRA. Funnel 25 opps 8 term sheets $1B 2025 value.

Key assumptions for FY2024 $4.8-5.0B revenue 12-15% growth: NovaTRK 25-30% U.S. share peak $2.2B, EMA Q4 2024 launches H1 2025 20% ex-U.S. 18% CAGR 15-20% ASP haircut France/Italy, China Fosun NMPA mid-2025 $400M by 2027 30%+ growth. Pipeline bispecifics $850M R&D Ph3 NAVIGATE NovaBispec-101 Q2 2025 75% PFS, 25% PoS $1.5B incremental. Ops gross 82-84% Singapore 70% API, SG&A 22% AI HCP 15% spend cut, $1.2B Editas CRISPR milestones $500M repurchase net cash $2.8B.

Risks: clinical/reg 70-80% derail NovaTRK CREST-OS negative 20-30% sales $1.5B downside, EMA CMC delays $300M FY25. Competition Bayer/Turning Point 5% erosion to 15%, NovaGSD Pompe biosimilars 25% cliff subQ Ph2 offset. Pricing IRA 70-80% WAC 45% rebates to 50% 200bps, Europe IQWiG 30% delays. Macro biologics inflation 12% debt +50bps $7.5M, Indian CDMOs Red Sea 4-6 weeks, U.S.-China Fosun $200M down. M&A overpay 5.5x multiples dilution, turnover 18%. Exogenous pandemics IRA rollbacks 10% toggle. Diversified 45% three assets 30% partnerships 25% pipeline $800M revolver.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Rachel Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

**Dr. Rachel Patel, Chief Medical Officer:**
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, we've hit 95% enrollment ahead of schedule across pivotal trials with adaptive designs and 250+ global sites. We expect upcoming milestones like Phase 3 toplines and BLA filings.

Next, Dr. Kevin Morales will provide an update on our research pipeline.

**Dr. Kevin Morales, Chief Scientific Officer:**
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Thank you, Dr. Harlan, and good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a transformative quarter for BioNova Therapeutics, I'm excited to dive into clinical trial updates across phase progressions, key data readouts, and regulatory milestones. Pipeline focused on immuno-oncology, rare genetic disorders, neurodegenerative, six late-stage, 95% enrollment.

Flagship INP-301 bispecific T-cell engager solid tumors NSCLC/HNSCC: Ph2b INNOVATE-2 topline 320 patients 52% ORR 10mg vs 28% chemo p<0.0001 PFS HR 0.62 9.2 vs 5.1 months OS 28% reduction, Gr3+ CRS 12% 4% disc. Ph3 INNOVATE-3 vs pembro 1050 frontline NSCLC 40% enrolled topline Q4 2025 FDA BTD End-Ph2 BLA H2 2026 EMA protocol Japan PMDA, $40B PD-1 slice post-2028 cliffs.

INP-452 DMD gene therapy Ph2 EMBARK 48 boys 35% NSAA p=0.002 22% milestones 41% NT-proBNP drop AAV9 2.5x expression low immunogenicity. Pivotal Ph3 EMBARK-2 200 sham adaptive RMAT BLA mid-2026 20 Brazil/Aus sites orphan incentives Pfizer $2B benchmark co-dev talks.

INP-789 HD ASO Ph2a SIGNAL 36 patients 48% CSF mHTT 20mg 22% UHDRS slow intrathecal LNP. Ph2b 180 enrolled interim Q1 2025 pediatric ENROLL-HD Fast Track Orphan PRIME, cleaner safety vs Ionis Ph3 H1 2025 $5B market.

Earlier: INP-112 IPF JAK inh Ph1b 67% FVC Takeda $50M opt-in Ph2 Q2 2025. INP-567 CRISPR CAR-T MM Ph1 MD Anderson 90% expansion.

Summary $1.2B milestones peak $8B+ 2030, 18-month runway $300M ATM.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

**Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial:**
Thank you, Dr. Morales. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding with 20% growth. We are seeing strong uptake in NovaTRK and GeneFix across key market segments. Our marketing campaigns are proving effective in driving KOL adoption and payer coverage through RWE and AI targeting. Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our new product launches and impressive market share gains. 2024 pivotal with three launches immuno-oncology rare disease. Flagship ONCObis-301 bispecific PD-1/Claudin-18.2 gastric/GEJ U.S. Q4 2023 FDA accel EMA Q1 NMPA recent.

Q3 $285M net smashing $200M guidance 180% QoQ from $102M FY2024 $1.1B peak $3.2B 2028 up $2.7B. 85% U.S. commercial coverage 90 days PBMs MD Anderson MSK endorsements. IQVIA NBRx 22% U.S. Claudin+ up from 12% vs Tecentriq Opdivo-Yervoy Europe 18% 45% Rx moM CLARITY 28% ORR. U.S. 62% $177M Europe 25% $71M ex-China 13% $37M China tenders $50M H2.

GENEfix-42 SMA AAV Q1 FDA $112M Q3 150% seq 1200 patients 20% >Zolgensma 14% WW share $2.1M 15% discount STAR 92% 24mo SMN.

IMMUNOblock-7 BTK CLL $68M 220% QoQ 11% 3L vs Imbruvica Brukinsa Ph3 frontline Q4 2025 TAM $8B.

Precision Launch AI PROACT 35% HCP accuracy Singapore 120kL 50k patients. Biosimilars shift $50B IO bispecifics ASCO PFS>ADCs. U.S. 95% GTN 22% VBP OS rebates. Europe HTA NICE Italy 25% cost reduction. Asia PMDA Q3 WuXi. Q4 40-50% YoY 25%+ share supply plasmid Merck ESMO 18mo cash $1.2B loan M&A.

Next, Tom Reilly will discuss our manufacturing operations.

**Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing:**
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly with expansions at Singapore handling 70% NovaTRK API, reducing dependencies amid shortages, and North Carolina optimizations for GeneFix. We've scaled bioreactors and secured CMO capacity via Lonza for cell therapies. We are focused on efficiencies driving gross margins to 82-84%, green chemistry cutting emissions 30%, and resilience to disruptions like Red Sea via diversified CDMOs.

Finally, Maria Lopez will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

**Maria Lopez, Head of Regulatory Affairs:**
Thank you, Tom. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies, securing BTD for INP-301, RMAT for INP-452, Fast Track/Orphan for INP-789, EMA PRIME reviews, PMDA fast-tracks, and alignments on Ph3 designs. Recent EMA acceptance for NovaTRK, NMPA clearances, and proactive JCA/HTA dossiers position us for multiple BLA filings H2 2026 and launches H1 2025.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Dr. Harlan.

**Dr. James Harlan, CEO:**
Thank you, Maria. In closing my overview, our strategic priorities center on pipeline acceleration in IO, cardiometabolics, rare diseases with $1.2B Q3 R&D 22% revenues. Oncology OncoTarget-301 Ph3 NSCLC 42% PFS vs Keytruda BLA YE PDUFA Q4 2025 $3.5B peak HCC ADC. NeoVera GLP-1 150k scripts 8% oral share $450M 2024 $1.2B 2027 weekly CVOT Q2. GeneXpert-AAV SMA Ph2/3 complete < $1.8M IRA CMS PRIME China. AI AlphaFold 35% timelines Tempus $250M RWE 20-30% responses.

Commercial ViraShield PCSK9 22% $1.1B ImmunoGuard HIV 15% to 2032 subQ. U.S. 62% 24% TRx CVS UnitedHealth Europe 14% AMNOG 85% Germany China double $180M EM 10%. Pricing 82% net copay 340B.

Portfolio M&A Aura $2.1B ALS/DMD $1B NPV 18 programs 7 Ph3 ROIC>15% $300-400M IRA clawbacks biosimilars $250M adalimumab.

Outlook FY24 $11.0-11.3B 17-20% core EPS $6.80-7.00 Q4 $2.9-3.0B margins +150bps. 2025-2028 15-18% CAGR $8-10B launches 20%+ EPS 10% R&D. Inflation 3% hedged PDUFA slips 90% comp GLP-1 moat.

We will now open the call for questions.

**Operator:**
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**Mike Johnson, Goldman Sachs:**
Thanks. Great quarter. On NovaTRK ramp and EMA approval assumptions, any updates on HTA timelines in Europe?

**Dr. James Harlan, CEO:**
Thanks, Mike. Sarah, want to take that?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Sure. We're modeling EMA approval Q4 2024 with H1 2025 launches in Germany/UK, 15-20% ASP haircut in France/Italy aligned with Tagrisso precedents, Europe 20% ex-U.S. revenue 18% CAGR. HTA negotiations progressing, value dossiers with partitioned survival supporting premium status.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**Laura Kim, JPMorgan:**
On pipeline, thoughts on INP-301 Ph3 enrollment speed and BTD impact?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Dr. Morales?

**Dr. Kevin Morales, Chief Scientific Officer:**
Thanks, Laura. 40% enrolled in two months for INNOVATE-3 vs pembro, BTD accelerates review, End-Ph2 aligned BLA H2 2026, positions for $40B PD-1 share post-Keytruda cliff.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**David Lee, Morgan Stanley:**
Pricing dynamics for GeneFix under IRA, any OBA expansions?

**Lisa Grant, Head of Commercial:**
Yes, David. OBAs cover 15% lives tying to motor milestones, copay caps preserved revenue, CMS negotiations for < $1.8M one-time, RWE supporting expansions like Zolgensma.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Patel, Barclays:**
BD pipeline, any color on next tuck-ins or Asia focus?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
Active funnel 25 opps, tuck-ins <500M like SynthoGenix ADCs, 35% Asia for IRA hedge, WuXi tech transfer, targeting $1B value 2025 in PROTACs multispecifics.

**Operator:**
Our next question from Alex Wong with Citi.

**Alex Wong, Citi:**
Patent strategies for Zylara post-2028?

**Sarah Chen, CFO:**
LCM label obesity +3 years, oral Ph2 2029, pediatric 6 months, thickets to 2031, offsetting 40-60% cliff with $15B pipeline.

**Dr. James Harlan, CEO:**
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

**Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations:**
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the BioNova Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

**Operator:**
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
